rationale: All eight tasks have findings, and the core of the report is now backed by official sources. Ofgem and Citizens Advice cover contract types, renewal, switching and broker rules. The Energy Ombudsman covers broker disputes. HMRC covers CCL and VAT. NESO and Ofgem cover TNUoS, BSUoS and the Renewables Obligation. Elexon covers half-hourly settlement. GOV.UK covers ESOS phase 4 and BICS. The T6 to T8 follow-ups closed the main gaps: official network-charge sources, Ofgem switching and objection guidance, the 2022 termination-notice change, ESOS phase 4 dates, and a check on current support. No more research is allowed, and the remaining gaps are narrow enough to state as limitations: DUoS, FiT, CfD and capacity market detail; supplier financial-resilience checks; UIA code of practice; the full list of switch-objection grounds; the back-billing cap; the ESOS phase 4 thresholds; contract capacity; and green-claim verification. The evidence is not contradictory. The earlier findings F5/F6 and F27 fit together, with F27 giving the later rule change.
caveats: F27 supersedes the 2015 notice position in the Ofgem factsheet (S17): since 1 Oct 2022 suppliers cannot require microbusinesses to give notice to switch, except on evergreen contracts, which keep the 30-day limit and 5-working-day acknowledgement (F5, F6).

F9 and F4 (Ofgem, April 2024) supersede the narrower microbusiness-only broker-fee disclosure in F14 and F28. Disclosure applies to all non-domestic customers for contracts signed on or after 1 Oct 2024. Ofgem described some measures as 'expected', so say they were announced rather than confirmed in force.

F29 supersedes F20 for current ESOS requirements. Phase 4 qualification date is 31 Dec 2026 and notification deadline is 5 Dec 2027. The 'large undertaking' thresholds were not read and must be stated as a limitation, along with the remaining phase 3 progress update due 5 Dec 2026.

F25 is a synthesis. The official sources do not confirm GLCG's claims on how non-commodity costs are bundled or passed through in fixed versus pass-through contracts (F3, F11), so state those claims as resting on GLCG, a commercial broker blog.

F3, F2, F21 and F11 rest on GLCG (commercial). This covers the pros and cons of each contract type, the 3–6 month early-renewal advice, and the bill component breakdown, including the claim that non-commodity costs can exceed half the bill.
F18: the Elexon MHHS material is industry-facing and does not say what customers should do. Contract capacity and half-hourly meter preparation are not covered, so state this as a limitation.
F19: the Ofgem REGO page does not tell businesses how to verify a green tariff, and no ASA or CMA guidance on green claims was read. State this as a limitation.
F22: TNUoS figures are initial 2027/28 forecasts (May 2026), not final tariffs. The £96.85 figure refers to an average consumer bill, not a business bill. Final tariffs are due by 31 Jan 2027.

F23, F24: no official page on how suppliers pass BSUoS, TNUoS or RO costs into business contracts was read. DUoS, FiT, CfD levy and capacity market are not covered by official sources, so state this as a limitation.

F26, F8: no Ofgem or Energy Ombudsman source gives the non-domestic switching timeline. The 5-working-day figure is from Citizens Advice only. Only debt is cited as an example of a supplier objection, and the full list of grounds was not read.
F28: SLC 7A.4 and the dates of the 2022 reforms come from a law-firm summary (CMS, S18), not licence text or the Ofgem decision. The SLC reference for the termination-notice change is unconfirmed.
The 12-month back-billing cap was not confirmed from any opened page and should not be stated as fact.
F10: the microbusiness definition differs slightly between Ofgem pages (Euro versus pound turnover, 'under' versus 'up to'). Advise checking the current licence definition.

F12, F13: the CCL rate table was last updated 27 Nov 2025. The VAT notice's temporary zero rate is described for domestic and 'other qualifying use' and cannot be confirmed to cover ordinary business electricity, so do not tell businesses it applies.

F30: BICS is a targeted scheme for eligible manufacturers, sourced only from a GOV.UK press release (applications by 30 Nov, support from April 2027). No general successor to the Energy Bill Discount Scheme was found, so state this as 'not found' rather than 'does not exist'. The Energy Bill Relief Scheme reference in the VAT notice covers 1 Oct 2022 to 31 Mar 2023 and is historical.

F16: Energy Ombudsman small-business eligibility (from 19 Dec 2024) is taken from the broker page. It does not clarify whether more than one criterion must be met, and larger businesses may not qualify.

F17: no source covers supplier financial-resilience checks. Say only that Ofgem notes suppliers may choose customers by size or credit rating, and that Citizens Advice advises not to switch until the account has moved after a supplier failure.
F15: Citizens Advice names the DRO in one page and only the Energy Ombudsman and UIA in another. UIA code-of-practice details were not read.

Several Ofgem and Citizens Advice pages (S1, S3, S8, S10, S16) show no publication date. Present them as read on the access date (4 Nov 2026) and note that the Ofgem TPI guidance (S9) dates from October 2022.
